User is planning a flexible round-trip economy trip from Washington, DC (likely IAD) to San Francisco (SFO) in a few weeks. Target budget ~$400, but willing to spend ~$410–430 for a nonstop IAD–SFO flight. They have United MileagePlus Premier Gold status and want to wait for a sale; they may set alerts themselves via United/Google Flights/Skyscanner, but I cannot create alerts or monitor fares. United route distance is about 2,465 miles, but flight-mile earnings vary by fare and current elite earning rules; do not promise totals. Premier Platinum qualification is currently generally 75,000 PQMs or 90 PQS per calendar year, subject to United’s official requirements.

User previously considered DC–LAX using miles, possibly transferring Chase Ultimate Rewards points to United (generally 1:1 in 1,000-point increments, potentially taking hours/days), but current trip is SFO.

For expense tracking, user currently uses a spreadsheet and is considering Expensify. They want advice on whether its free plan is sufficient or premium is worthwhile. Recommend starting free for personal expenses and upgrading only if advanced workflows, card/bank reconciliation, or team/accounting features are ne
trajectory: User is planning a trip from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles (LAX) and wants a one-way economy United award ticket using MileagePlus miles. They have just reached 20,000 United miles and say this qualifies them for Premier Silver status (this may warrant confirmation under United’s current qualification rules; status alone does not necessarily mean booking a specific award). They are considering transferring Chase Ultimate Rewards points to United to cover the ticket and asked how to do that. Need remind them that Chase transfers are generally 1:1 to MileagePlus, in 1,000-point increments, through Chase’s “Travel Partners” transfer flow, and can take several hours to several days, so transfer enough time before departure. They also want an estimate of award-ticket taxes and fees for DC–LAX. Exact fees must be obtained at United checkout; prior generic estimates should not be relied upon. United award pricing, fare classes, close-in/change/cancellation rules, and taxes vary and have changed, so verify live rather than quote fixed mileage or fee amounts. Clarify whether “DC” means DCA or IAD, travel date, nonstop/preference, and desired departure time.
